question: Pupils read a text on the heart and blood; some were prompted to explain each line to themselves. What happened?
options: They learned less, being slowed down
answer: They understood it better. Chi and colleagues asked eighth-graders to read a biology text on the circulatory system, half of them prompted to explain each line to themselves. The self-explainers built more correct models of how blood circulates, and those who explained the most learned the most. Explaining showed them where their picture had holes.
move: Explain each step to yourself as if a sceptic were listening.
ask: When I read something hard, do I stop to explain each step to myself, or just keep going?
trap: Stopping at every line seems to slow learning down.
reference: Chi, de Leeuw, Chiu and LaVancher, Eliciting self-explanations improves understanding, Cognitive Science, 1994
